internal.title: SEV2: Checkout Service Errors Due to Payment Service Token Failures
internal.body:
At 11:25 UTC, an alert was triggered for high error rates in the checkout service. Initial diagnosis identified a high error rate (25%) in the payment service caused by invalid token errors, which injected errors into the checkout process. The checkout service itself showed elevated error rates (23.75%) and latency (400 ms) related to failed card charges due to these payment service errors.

At 11:45 UTC, the ops team disabled the paymentFailure flag to mitigate the issue. Post-action verification showed error rates dropped from 25% to 0.2%, confirming recovery.

Actions taken:
- Disabled paymentFailure flag to stop error injection in payment service.

Impact:
- Checkout errors and increased latency affecting customer transactions.

Recovery verified at 11:45 UTC with error rates normalized.

Next steps include reviewing token validation processes in payment service to prevent recurrence.

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment processing errors
external.body: Between 11:25 and 11:45 UTC, some customers experienced issues completing checkout due to errors in the payment processing system. The issue was identified and resolved by disabling a problematic feature causing payment failures. Normal service resumed shortly after, and customers should no longer experience checkout problems.

output.summary: Checkout service experienced elevated error rates due to payment service token validation errors causing failed card charges.
output.impact: Customers experienced checkout failures and increased latency during the incident window, impacting transaction completion.
output.root_cause: Error injection in the payment service caused by invalid token errors led to high error rates and cascading failures in the checkout service.
output.resolution: Disabled the paymentFailure flag in the payment service, stopping error injection and restoring normal service operation.

lessons.lesson: Implement stricter validation and monitoring of token handling to prevent error injection affecting downstream services.
lessons.applies_when: When payment service error rates spike due to token validation errors causing downstream service impact.

action_items: Review and improve token validation logic in payment service.
Enhance monitoring for early detection of token-related errors.
Conduct a post-incident review with payment and checkout teams to identify process improvements.
